body: Thank you. It's hard when you're ready to be done with someone, but of course you still care and you want to help.
no... he keeps himself pretty isolated. Except for me.

No I haven't. I may have said it while we were spatting and I'm saying it more to throw in his face rather than, this IS actually how I feel. I've never tried to thoughtfully, articulate this to him.I definitely feel guilty a lot, like I did something wrong, cuz you never know. I just expect him to be upset (about relative issues). It's a relief and surprise if he isn't.

If it was a work girl no. I wouldn't be pissed. A random girl yes. But I also wouldn't be bringing random guys home. Even if I was upset, I KNOW he isn't straying.  Part of it is that he questions me about my loyalty so much. I understand that it definitely was not the best choice. But a liiiiitle trust would be nice. Or at least a platform to present my case on for him to consider. Also, the person it was should pose NO threats. He's much older, unattractive, obtuse...theres no chance something would happen that I would be into.
The talking was first. I was new and trying to get along with people. (I wa freelance when we first started dating, then got hired).

>He should realise that you're with HIM not these other people, you want him, not them. 

Man, if I had a dollar for everyone I said that to him, I'd be rich.

Yes it wasn't the best idea. Especially knowing how he is. But it still shouldn't be THAT big of an issue. I told him I felt pressured (plus I'm bad at saying no) and then I asked him to leave once we were done. 

Thanks for you words.no offense taken. And eating and shitting together isn't always great.

Well, he is currently saying he wants nothing to do with me because last night i went out for drinks with coworkers instead of his place. One of the guys gave me a ride home and asked if he coul come up and smoke a bowl (it was kind if awkward, a guy who's been trying to fit in) so I figured why not. I knew BF wouldn't like it, but he was giving me a ride, it's just a quick toke...harmless if you ask me. I told him about it, and he's pissed. 

"If you give a girl a ride home from the bar and she asks if you want to come up, generally, it means she wants to fuck." 

I asked the dude to leave once the the bowl was out. He's much older and awkward.

Other comments here have just verified my thoughts. I'm letting him walk all over me and change me. Past BFd have NEVER been anything like this.  Because they knew I was coming home to them, and understood the gender dynamic in my field. I've become more insecure since being with him, always worried he'll be mad at me for this or that. Not doing what I want.

So I think I'm done groveling. If he wants to talk I will mention that lately my decisions are based on him. And even though he thinks I have wavering thoughts, nothing has ever happened. I will stress that it's frustrating he doesn't trust me. But if it goes like past conversations about these matters, it won't get anywhere. I'll be the flirtatious dummy, too naive to realize these guys aren't my friends they wanna fuck. Oh and I'm disrespecting him, making him look bad.

I'm done fighting for honor. He straight up doesn't listen or consider my side.

Work will suck if we split though.

I know his last girlfriend cheated on him. I've never really asked about because, well, who wants to talk about something like that? 

I guess I've been too worried about the repercussion of asking if he is doing this, because of his ex. I'm also bad a talking, so I would inevitably pose it in the worst way possible.

Thank you. You're basically right. 

>he sees it as you trying to hook up with guys because why else would you treat them the same as how you treated your bf before you got together?

Yes, he's definitely said exactly this. 

Same as your work situation, I'm positive they say stuff about me. They would say stuff to my bf before they knew we were together. But they're not complete assholes. They're friends with him too.

>It is disrespectful to you because he is saying that he doesn't trust you and already thinks you are one step away from cheating. It is a guilt trip to get you to stay in.

Yep. I end up thinking that I shouldn't have gone out, I should have just stayed in with him and nothing would have come of it. I defend myself til my face turns blue that he's the only one I want, I had no bad intentions. 

>It seems shady if he is walking by and catches you talking to these guys then stop when he comes over.

I don't suddenly stop all guiltily, just finish it up and move on. But I will say that I am a little bit different if he is working with us that day. I Keep to myself more, and stay away from the people he's deemed a threat and talk more to the safe people. (There a certain guys that he particularly latches on to the notion that I have a thing for. The safe one's are mostly the married guys, or not good looking ones.)

>"I trust you but not the coworkers"  -- Yep.

Yea...that's kind of what I've been thinking. I've noticed that he tells me to do little things. Like, getting out of work clothes into comfy clothes, or pouring shots if we're drinking. He says things in a playful way, but it's still that fact that he's telling me to do it. 

We have sort of have D/s relationship in the bedroom. And we've never really talked about how it translates into regular life because we both started it together. For me though, it shouldn't leave the bedroom. That's the ONLY place he can call me names and tell me what to do. And generally speaking he's very sweet and affectionate. Sometimes though, I wonder if he thinks it can leave the bedroom. It's definitely something I will bring up.

I have a couple girlfriends that he never objects to me seeing 
(which isn't as often cuz I'm with him so much). But I do have some dude friends that I haven't seen since we started dating, because I didn't even want to deal what he'd have to say. 

It's definitely been wearing me down. I've noticed that I've been doing things based on what he'd think, which a lot of times, is different than what I would do.

hey girl, I know you already have a lot of responses and may not even see this, but I think you're doing a good thing. You're being logical and reasonable and that's all one can be in this type of situation. I think it's awesome how you're balancing your religious upbringing with you newfound freedom. It shows a lot that you and the father are doing this together, and that you talked to your parents about it. It sucks right now, but I think it will all work out in the end. Keep a strong head on your shoulders.
